subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**nothing**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The passage describes the catastrophic damage to the ship: "six great holes were made in the steel," and water "rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet," rendering "The steel doors... useless."
 
• Given this extensive and uncontrollable damage, Captain Smith would understand that the situation was dire and beyond remedy.
 
• "**Nothing**" (कुछ भी नहीं) logically completes the sentence, implying that no action or force could now save the ship from sinking. This leads to his subsequent action of sending a distress call.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

Complete Passage: *The ship struck the iceberg (1) **with **__its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2) __**moments**__, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3) __**useless**__. Captain Smith soon understood that (4)__nothing__ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "enemies"** – This word is completely out of context. The ship is damaged by an iceberg, not enemies.
 
• **Option 2: "all"** – "All could save the ship" does not make sense in the context of a sinking ship.
 
• **Option 4: "everything"** – "Everything could save the ship" implies that the ship was salvageable, which directly contradicts the severity of the damage and the subsequent distress call.
